rechecks.argument: I tried to move the date. The 2020 interim analysis is excluded by the criterion. MAPS's release of 2021-05-03 reports a significant reduction on the primary PTSD-severity measure versus placebo with therapy (p<0.0001); Nature Medicine published the paper on 2021-05-10; ClinicalTrials.gov results were first submitted 2021-08-18 and posted 2021-09-16. I found no earlier public report: MAPS's own 2021-05-21 summary says the results were announced May 3 and published May 10. The release came from MAPS, the parent of sponsor MAPS PBC, which the criterion accepts as the sponsor's topline release. Occurred on 2021-05-03 stands.

The recorded resolution counts the FTC stipulation over data and cancellation practices as a settlement over Cerebral's 'business practices'. Under the same reading an earlier qualifying settlement exists. On 2023-12-28 the New York Attorney General announced an agreement under which Cerebral, Inc. pays $200,000 in penalties and $540,162 in restitution to 16,552 New Yorkers for a burdensome cancellation process, charges after cancellation and manipulated online reviews. A state attorney general is a named enforcement agency, and the criterion fixes an agency settlement's date by the agency press release. I found no earlier qualifying action: the N.D. Iowa qui tam was dismissed without judgment, and the DOJ and FTC matters closed later. The first-true date moves from 2024-04-15 to 2023-12-28; the state is unchanged.

rechecks.argument: PubMed shows no qualifying multi-daily theta-burst RCT in depression from 2022-07-12 to 2024-07-10: Wilkening 2022 and Li 2023 missed their primary endpoints; Kong 2023 was a non-inferiority trial of V1 versus DLPFC with no sham arm; Huang 2024, Zhang 2024 and Mallik 2022 were not significant. So Sheline et al. (JAMA Psychiatry online 2024-07-10; 10 sessions a day for 5 days; MADRS -14.75 versus sham, P<.001) is the first positive RCT, but its population is treatment-refractory bipolar depression. The criterion says "a depressive disorder"; DSM-5 files bipolar disorders in a separate chapter, while the proposition says "for depression" and the registered conditions include treatment-resistant depression. If bipolar depression is excluded, the next candidate is Ramos et al. (online 2025-03-05; TRD; 3 sessions a day for 15 weekdays), outside the "about five days" reading. The readings differ by eight months; the criterion does not settle it.

I looked for an earlier Magnus announcement of commercial availability or of a first commercial patient. The Business Wire list of Magnus releases and the company's own release index show nothing between the 2023-10-23 CPT-code release, which only anticipates hospital claims once the codes take effect on 2024-07-01, and the 2024-04-30 'Commercial Launch' release that names the first customer sites. CMS's FY 2024 IPPS final rule records the applicant telling CMS that SAINT 'will be commercially available on April 15, 2024', and UAMS's 'first in the nation to offer' release is dated 2024-06-11; neither is a Magnus press release, the only source the criterion accepts. FDA clearance (2022-09-06) and the OLO trial (2023-07-20) are excluded. Occurred on 2024-04-30 stands.

The 2023-01-05 release (PR Newswire and mapsbcorp.com) says MAPP2 'met both the primary endpoint as measured by the change from baseline in CAPS-5 and the key secondary endpoint', but it gives no p-value and never says 'statistically significant'; the parent MAPS post of the same day gives no efficacy statistic at all. One could push the date to the Nature Medicine paper (2023-09-14, P<0.001) or the ClinicalTrials.gov results posting (2023-10-11). I do not: a sponsor's statement that a trial 'met' its prespecified primary endpoint is the standard report that the prespecified test reached significance, the publication confirmed it, and the criterion accepts significance 'as reported by the sponsor'. No earlier disclosure exists; the 2022-11-17 completion release only promised topline results in Q1 2023. Occurred on 2023-01-05 stands.

The recorded date relies on NCT05163496 being 'registered as Phase 3'. Its ClinicalTrials.gov version history shows otherwise: the versions of 2021-12-06, 2021-12-17 and 2022-07-13 list Phase 1/Phase 2, and the July 2022 version already carries the actual start date 2022-03-03; the Phase 3 label first appears in the 2023-05-17 version, fourteen months after the start. So on 2022-03-03 a trial registered as Phase 1/2 started, and no psilocybin trial registered as Phase 3 had started. The first psilocybin trial registered as Phase 3 when it started is COMPASS's COMP005 (NCT05624268), posted 2022-11-22 as Phase 3 with actual start 2023-01-24; no sponsor first-patient release predates that, and the ClinicalTrials.gov Phase 3 search shows no other candidate before it. The first-true date moves to 2023-01-24; the state is unchanged.

rechecks.argument: I argued that the 2023 proposal was never revised, withdrawn or replaced: no withdrawal notice exists, and the 2025-01-17 NPRM never uses the words withdraw, supersede or replace. The text of 90 FR 6541 defeats this. It is issued under the same RIN 1117-AB40 and docket DEA-407; it says DEA 'reevaluated its approach and determined that the best course of action was to proceed with the promulgation of a Special Registration rule', which 'no longer contains an in-person medical examination requirement for certain substances' nor the 30-day supply limit; and its Regulatory Alternatives section lists 'finalizing the proposed March 2023 General Telemedicine NPRM' as a rejected alternative. That is a new proposal that supersedes the 2023 one. The same-day VA final rule (90 FR 6523; RIN 1117-AB40; docket DEA-2023-0029) partially finalizes the rulemaking on different terms, also on 2025-01-17. Nothing earlier in the docket qualifies. Occurred on 2025-01-17 stands.

The criterion fixes the date at the DEA announcement date when it is earlier than Federal Register publication. The resolver used DEA's press release of 2023-05-09 on the temporary rule (filed 2023-05-09, published 2023-05-10, effective 2023-05-11). DEA made an earlier public announcement: the Administrator's statement of 2023-05-03 (dea.gov, dated in its URL and quoted by K&L Gates and trade press; dea.gov refuses automated fetches) said DEA had received a record 38,000 comments and 'we have decided to extend the current flexibilities while we work to find a way forward'. Read as the DEA announcement of the extension, the first-true date is 2023-05-03. Read strictly, the statement announced a decision but no rule or order, and the rule was first announced on 2023-05-09. The criterion does not say which announcement counts. The state is unaffected; the date needs a ruling.

I tried to move the date to DEA's announcement of 2023-10-06 ('DEA and HHS Extend Telemedicine Flexibilities through 2024') or to the public-inspection posting. Unlike E-0014, this criterion names only the Federal Register publication date. The Federal Register API gives publication_date 2023-10-10 for 88 FR 69879 (document 2023-22406, docket DEA-407), a temporary rule that extends the full flexibilities through 2024-12-31, beyond the 2023-11-11 end date and the 2024-11-11 grace period set by the first extension of 2023-05-10. It is a temporary rule, not a permanent replacement. The third (2024-11-19) and fourth (2025-12-31) extensions do not change the first-true date. Occurred on 2023-10-10 stands.

I tested whether the date should be the publication date (2023-08-28) or the display date (2023-08-01) rather than the effective date, and whether the approval was final. The FY 2024 IPPS/LTCH PPS final rule (88 FR 58640) states 'we are finalizing that the maximum new technology add-on payment for a case involving the use of the SAINT Neuromodulation System is $12,675.00 for FY 2024', with cases identified by ICD-10-PCS X0Z0X18, and 'DATES: This final rule is effective October 1, 2023.' The criterion names the effective date, so 2023-10-01 is correct. No earlier IPPS rule approved an NTAP for SAINT; FDA clearance came 2022-09-06, after the FY 2023 application cycle. The rule also records the applicant's statement that SAINT would be commercially available on 2024-04-15, which bears on the newness period, not on approval. Occurred on 2023-10-01 stands.
